steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ What symbol should be used to multiply the Player sprite’s y-acceleration, so that it is a negative value?


Solution:

Code should be added in the if condition of the onEvent function set the sprite’s y-acceleration to a negative value: mySprite.ay = spriteAcceleration * -1. 


Code should be added in the else condition of the onEvent function set the sprite’s y-acceleration back to a positive value: mySprite.ay = spriteAcceleration.


Ask the ninja:

❓What operator should be used to check if one of multiple conditions are true?


Solution:

Inside the if condition of the onHitWall event, a Boolean OR operator || should be added, followed by a second tileAtLocationEquals that checks for the spikeTileDown tile asset.


Ask the ninja:

❓ What sprite kind should be destroyed when the project resets? 


Solution:

The destroyAllSpritesOfKind function should be updated in the top of the setStars function definition, set to the Food sprite kind.
steps.instructions:
Fix the bugs in the code to create a working platformer game!


The on A button pressed event should be used to change the Player sprite’s y-acceleration (ay) to different values, depending on whether the Player sprite is upside down or not.


The project should be reset whenever the Player sprite overlaps with either one of the two spike tiles.


All of the Food sprites should be destroyed, whenever the project is reset.


Use the functions in the code menu and the code completion tool to create a working version of this 2D platformer project!

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 3 of Brown Belt! In this level, you’ll learn more about using physics and Boolean values to control game conditions in 2D platform tilemap projects. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level 3:

badges.title: Taking Control
badges.description: Control the way sprites move and appear on screen in a 2D tilemap project in JavaScript.

badges.title: Gravity of the Situation
badges.description: Use physics to control a sprite’s velocity and acceleration in a 2D tilemap project in JavaScript.

badges.title: Checkin’ it Twice
badges.description: Check for a specific tile image at a specific tilemap location.

badges.title: While You’re At It…
badges.description: Use a while loop to make something happen while a certain condition is true.

badges.title: And the Winner Is…
badges.description: Create a function that uses Boolean operators and values to determine which sprite image to use.

badges.title: Well-Rounded Character
